about.title: Dixon Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Dixon sits at a crossroads of regional travel, with I-80 traffic feeding into local corridors like Rt 113, West A Street, and Pitt School Road. Public crash records show 77 injury collisions and 92 people hurt in the most recent final year, with Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the heaviest concentration of reported crashes. Whether you were stopped at a light on West A Street or merging near the I-80 interchange, the aftermath of a collision can mean medical bills, missed work, and a lot of unanswered questions. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect injured Dixon residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to talk, and the attorneys in our network only get paid if you recover compensation. The sooner you speak with someone, the sooner evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness statements can be preserved before it disappears.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon After a Dixon Crash

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a personal injury claim in California, but if a government entity — like a city road crew or Caltrans — was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting to speak with someone could cost you your right to file at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You Fast
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but the other side's insurer will look for any reason to shift blame onto you. An attorney can help make sure your side of the story, and the evidence supporting it, doesn't get lost.

items.title: No Cap Means Every Detail of Your Recovery Matters
items.desc: California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so a thorough accounting of how the crash has affected your life matters. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out what your claim may be worth.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on I-80 or near Pitt School Road and I'm not sure who was at fault?
items.answer: That's common, especially on higher-traffic corridors like I-80 and Rt 113 where merging and speed differences play a role. An attorney can help gather police reports, traffic camera footage if available, and witness accounts to help clarify what happened. You don't need to have it all figured out before reaching out.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Dixon car accident?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That window can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, if a government entity like a public road agency was involved. Because evidence and memories fade quickly, it's wise to talk to someone sooner rather than later.
